evidence: MP lists the DC as Mod. Snow; non-technical glacier climb whose hardest ground is loose Class 2-3 scrambling on the Cleaver.
Alpine Grade III; slope ramps to 45-50 degrees and stays there to Liberty Cap; documented mostly as a ski descent, no ice grade given.
note: Sustained 45-50 degree steep snow with no published ice grade mapped to Class 3; the record's AI3 ice_grade is unsupported by any source found (left for review).

evidence: MP: Mod. Snow; SummitPost: Grade II, moderate glacier travel, ~30-35 degree Corridor.
note: MP 'Mod. Snow' (non-technical glacier) mapped to Class 2; alpine_grade III contradicted the record's own commitment II and sources' Grade II.

evidence: MP: Mod. Snow, Grade II; ~2,200 ft of sustained 40-45 degree couloir on 30-45 degree snow/ice, usually protected with pickets.
note: MP 'Mod. Snow' with a sustained 40-45 degree couloir mapped to Class 3 (steep snow, no published ice grade); record's AI2-3 is plausible in icy years but unsourced.

evidence: MP lists Fuhrer Thumb as Mod. Snow; SummitPost: narrower couloir west of the Finger, Grade II on 30-45 degree snow/ice, joining the Finger at ~11,500 ft.
note: MP 'Mod. Snow' plus a steeper, narrower couloir mapped to Class 3.

evidence: MP: AI1-2 Mod. Snow; Grade II with 35-50 degree snow and ice, exposed ledges protected with pickets.
MP lists Ingraham Glacier Direct as Mod. Snow; a crevassed glacier climb up the headwall with no rock and no ice grade.
note: MP 'Mod. Snow' mapped to Class 2; steeper 40-45 degree headwall sections in some years.

evidence: MP lists WI2-3; two steps of alpine ice in the Kautz chute are the crux; the rock step is a ~25 ft rappel or downclimb off the Wapowety Cleaver, not a 5th-class climb.

fix.rock_grade: Class 3-4 (short rock step, usually rappelled or downclimbed)

note: MP writes WI2-3; given as AI3 because it is glacier ice. Guides and the Mountaineers call the route Grade II.

evidence: No dedicated page found; the Kautz ice chute it climbs directly is WI2-3 on MP, and the record's own ice_grade puts the crux pitch at AI3.
MP: AI2-3 Steep Snow; crux is the ice of the Black Pyramid / upper ridge and the bergschrund below Liberty Cap.
MP Central Mowich Face: AI3-4 Steep Snow overall; original Grade III line takes a 40-50 degree snow ramp, the Grade IV variation has AI2-3 ice steps and 50-60 degree snow.
note: MP's overall AI3-4 includes harder variations (Shelf Exit, 65 degree ice); the documented ice steps on both standard variations are AI2-3. No source supports the record's '5th class (sections)' rock_grade.

evidence: First climbed 1948 (Molenaar, Craig); route listings give Alpine Grade III with ice to ~60 degrees; no published AI grade.
note: No ice grade exists; 60-degree serac ice mapped to AI3 as a best reading.

evidence: MP: 5.6 AI2-3 Steep Snow; trip reports name a ~15 ft 5.6 rock chimney/step through the rock band as the crux.
note: Also AI2-3 ice to 55 degrees.

evidence: MP: 5.5 AI1-2 Steep Snow, Grade IV+; a short loose rock section is the only rock, otherwise 50-55 degree gullies.
note: Also AI1-2 and 50-60 degree snow; the record's breakdown calls the rock 'loose 4th class'.

evidence: MP lists Tahoma Glacier as Mod. Snow: a crevassed glacier climb with no rock or ice grade.
note: MP 'Mod. Snow' mapped to Class 2.

evidence: MP grades the wall M5+ X, Grade V (a mixed grade); other sources say it is not technically hard by modern standards and the danger is the 300 ft serac band.
note: MP's only grade is mixed (M5+ X), which none of the three scales can hold; AI3 kept from the record's ice_grade as a best reading. Several ribs exist (East Rib, Central Rib, Brumal Buttress) and the record does not say which one.

evidence: MP: WI2 Mod. Snow, Grade II; 30-50 degree snow and ice for ~3,000 ft with small rock bands that can be bypassed.
Route descriptions: a short 8-ft low-fifth move at the flying-buttress col (Class 5 with low snow cover), then a Class 4 summit chimney often choked with snow/ice.
note: Low 5th with no number given, so 5.0; in high snow cover the crux reads as Class 4.

evidence: SummitPost: its only non-technical route is an exposed Class 3 gully of rock, heather and dirt on the SE side.
Trip reports via Airplane Lake: easy Class 3 scramble from the saddle; sections of Class 3, nothing difficult.
Three established scramble routes (Noyes Basin, Seattle Creek Basin, Low Divide); easiest route Class 3.
Seattle Creek Basin is one of three scramble routes; reaches the Noyes-Seattle ridge and goes around the rotten east side to the south peak; Class 3.
Trip report via the Southwest Couloir: Class 2-3 scramble to the craggy summit; easiest route on the peak rated Class 3.
SummitPost: ~1,800 ft confined couloir to Nooksack Ridge, a basic snow climb with some 3rd-4th class rock at the end.
note: The couloir itself is snow (sometimes ice); the 3rd-4th class finish sets the grade.

evidence: Trip report: Wall Street gully 30-35 degree snow, then the SE ridge was 'a straightforward Class 2 scramble except for 100 feet of exposed Class 3 traversing'.
SummitPost: from the Nooksack Cirque trail up the south slopes to the SE ridge, then a fractured class 3/4 ridge to the summit; reports mention two short Class 4 rock sections.
note: Sources describe the south-side line as joining the SE ridge for the finish rather than a separate southwest ridge.

evidence: MP: AI2-3 Steep Snow PG13, Grade III, ~2,000 ft; 50 degree choke and exposed traverse.
MP: 4th, AI1, Mod. Snow; Class 3-4 chimneys, steep snow at Winnie's Slide and Hell's Highway, Class 3-4 summit pyramid.
note: No source supports 5th-class steps; the 5th-class option is the separate SE Ridge finish. AI1 ice on Winnie's Slide late season.

evidence: 1939 Hennig-Trott route: glacier travel, ice up to 65 degrees, and some 5.6 rock on the east ridge of the summit pyramid.
note: Also steep ice to 65 degrees (record AI4); sources name no single crux, so YDS by default.

evidence: MP: AI2-3 Mod. Snow; 45-50 degree snow/ice face, summit pyramid options 4th class to 5.6.

note: No source found for the record's 5.7; only this collective 4th-5.6 statement.

evidence: Northwest Arete rated 5.7, Grade III, AI2+: bushwhacking, loose rock, moderate alpine ice and glacier; one climber reports little true 5.7.
note: Also AI2+. A separate 2007 'Northwest Arayete' (Grade III 5.9) exists; do not confuse them.

evidence: MP: Easy 5th, AI2-3, M4, Steep Snow; the route is known as an alpine ice climb through the Price Glacier seracs.
note: Ice is the route's defining crux; also easy 5th rock on the summit pyramid and M4 in some conditions.

evidence: MP: 3rd, Easy Snow; finishes with a Class 3 rock gully (snow early season) on the summit pyramid. Some sources call the pyramid Class 3-4.
note: MP preferred over the Class 3-4 elsewhere; the low-5th SE Ridge is a separate route.

evidence: MP: Easy Snow for the glacier; reaching the summit uses the summit pyramid, Class 3 on MP's Sulphide route.
note: MP 'Easy Snow' mapped to Class 2 for the glacier; the summit pyramid finish makes the crux Class 3.

evidence: MP: 5.3, 6 pitches; the Mountaineers say 5.3-5.7, with two unavoidable steps (5.6 and 5.7) if you stay on the true ridge.
note: Staying strictly on the ridge crest adds 5.6/5.7 steps.

evidence: MP: Grade III, WI2-3 with vertical ice passages and 300 ft of 60-70 degree ice; rock tops out at 5.2.
note: Also 5.2 rock on the SE corner buttress; ice is the harder climbing.

evidence: From Lake of the Angels: a typical Class 2 and 3 Olympic scramble, maybe 3+ in spots, on rotten rock.

Standard south-side route: no harder than 40-degree snow and 3rd-class rock; easy Class 3 to the summit.
